answers.q1: Cargo (Rust). No separate install step; cargo fetches dependencies during the build. Run: cargo build --workspace (add --locked to respect Cargo.lock). Rust >=1.96 is required, and CI uses the toolchain via rustup.
answers.q2: cargo test --workspace  (CI runs it with features, e.g. cargo test --verbose --workspace --features pcre2, and cargo test --verbose --workspace --features unstable-index)
answers.q3: cargo test --test integration regression  (tests/regression.rs is a module of the 'integration' test target, defined in Cargo.toml with path tests/tests.rs and autotests = false. There is no standalone 'regression' target, so the name filter 'regression' selects its tests.)
answers.q4: cargo fmt --all --check  (the CI rustfmt job). CI has no clippy step. The CI docs job also runs: RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --no-deps --document-private-items --workspace
answers.q5: Cargo.lock and fuzz/Cargo.lock (lockfiles; AGENTS.md says not to edit them by hand). No vendored directories found. The AGENTS.md block between the agentbrief:start/end markers is generated by `agentbrief sync`, so don't edit inside it.

q1.reason: Cargo, no separate install step, and `cargo build --workspace` fetches dependencies, matching the accepted build/fetch answer.

q2.reason: `cargo test --workspace` is an accepted command, and the extra CI feature variants are harmless detail.

q3.reason: `cargo test --test integration regression` matches the accepted command exactly and correctly explains the module/target relationship.

q4.reason: `cargo fmt --all --check` is accepted, it correctly states CI has no clippy, and the cargo doc command is a bonus.

q5.reason: It names Cargo.lock (accepted) and says no vendored directories; the generated AGENTS.md block is an extra detail that does not contradict the truth or hit any REJECT item.
